prospect.name: Nadav Roth
prospect.family_status: Has family in Israel; weekly Friday family dinners. No partner or children mentioned.
prospect.training_background: Played basketball almost daily until age 28, when an ankle injury ended it; has spent eight years looking for a replacement sport. Found the gym boring and switched to home training. Worked with a personal trainer on and off for three years — in person until it became too expensive, then a digital programme where he filmed himself for form corrections. That trainer moved to Thailand and stopped responding about eight months ago. Bought his first kettlebell a couple of months ago after seeing Trevor's videos and now trains at home for 25-30 minutes with no structured programme.
prospect.medical: Müller-Weiss disease in the left ankle, described by the prospect as a chronic disease; he cannot run. L5 lower-back injury sustained at age 14 from daily basketball training, which he still feels intermittently under exertion. Right shoulder pain lasting roughly four years that no clinician could diagnose, which he says he resolved himself two to three months before the call. Rates his stiffness 7-8 out of 10 and cannot touch the floor bending forward; tightest through hamstrings and hips.

signals: Lost his sport and his identity in it to injury — "I used to play basketball for a lot of years. Then I got injured in the ankle. And since then, I didn't find any other sports that I like... I think it's now eight years that I'm still searching"
Peak weight of 103 kg sixteen years ago, "I used to be really fat", now 90-91 kg and wanting 84-85
Frames it as unfinished business now that a long-standing blocker cleared: "now that I no longer have this pain in the shoulder that was keeping me back... now I can do the next jump"
Confidence is moderate because the dominant feature of the call is liquidity, not identity — he lives month to month with no savings and declined on price, which is not what usually stops a rebuilder

evidence: Explicit decline on the main offer: "I feel like it's really a whole package and it's a whole program that combines everything. But at the moment, I cannot afford it. So thank you."
Explicit decline on the downsell too: "I think it's not what I'm looking at right now at the moment" — because he wants the one-to-one element
No savings and no available funds disclosed: "I don't really save, you know, in each month. So it's living from a month to a month"

Counter-evidence for treating it as follow_up: the rep booked a check-in for a couple of months out and offered to send a free beginner video, and the prospect said "maybe in a couple of months, when I see my bank" — so a nurture path exists. But both tiers were declined on this call and there is no open decision, so it is scored lost rather than follow_up.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send a free beginner kettlebell video later the same day and put a check-in in the calendar for one to two months' time.

notable.note: The prospect disclosed a named chronic bone condition in the ankle (Müller-Weiss), an L5 spinal injury from adolescence and four years of undiagnosed shoulder pain. The rep's response when pitching the self-directed tier was to characterise all of it as not really injuries — "you don't even actually really have injuries at the moment, more so stiffnesses" — and he had already promised in the main presentation that "you're not going to be able to hurt yourself." No question was asked at any point about whether a doctor or physiotherapist had cleared loaded kettlebell training. The second Primal University downsell of the batch, again triggered by the prospect naming a budget.
